sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At its core, Color Fill is a simple yet challenging game where your goal is to fill an entire board with a single color. The game takes place on a grid, with each cell representing a square on the board. The game starts with a random color distribution, and your task is to change the color of each cell to match the target color. The twist is that you can only change the color of adjacent cells, which are horizontally or vertically adjacent to the cell you're currently selecting. This means that you'll need to think strategically about which cells to change and in what order to maximize your progress and minimize the number of moves required to fill the board.
         
         As you progress through the levels, the game introduces new elements that add an extra layer of complexity to the gameplay. For example, some levels may feature obstacles that block your path, while others may include power-ups that allow you to change multiple cells at once. The game also introduces new target colors, which can be challenging to achieve, especially on larger boards. To overcome these challenges, you'll need to develop a combination of problem-solving skills and strategic thinking.
         
         One of the key features of Color Fill is its use of a 'lock' mechanism. When a cell is changed to the target color, it becomes locked and cannot be changed again. This means that you'll need to think carefully about which cells to change and when to lock them in place to maximize your progress. The lock mechanism also adds an extra layer of strategy to the game, as you'll need to balance the need to fill the board with the need to lock in place cells that will help you achieve the target color.
